jobs.employer_name: Weierstraß-Institut für Angewandte Analysis und Stochastik (WIAS)
jobs.description: The Weierstrass Institute for Applied Analysis and Stochastics (WIAS) is an institute of the Forschungsverbund Berlin e.V. (FVB). The FVB comprises seven non-university research institutes in Berlin which are funded by the federal and state governments. The research institutes belong to the Leibniz Association.WIAS invites applications for aResearch Assistant Position (f/m/d)(Ref. 26/22)in the Research Group “Nonsmooth Variational Problems and Operator Equations”(Head: Prof. Dr. Michael Hintermüller),starting on January 1, 2027.Field of work:The successful candidate will work in the MATH+ project "DOC-TWIN: Duality-Based Error Control for Optimal Control Problems in Digital-Twin-Based Structural Health Monitoring". The project aims at developing a convex-duality-based framework for reliable error control in PDE-constrained optimal control problems motivated by digital-twin-based structural health monitoring.The Tasks include:- Developing and analyzing duality-based a posteriori error identities for PDE-constrained optimal control problems;- Deriving corresponding discrete a priori error identities and using them for convergence-rate analysis and certified nonlinear solver control;- Designing, implementing, and numerically validating finite element methods, including adaptive mesh-refinement strategies and suitable post-processing techniques;- Preparing scientific publications and presenting the results at workshops and conferences.**We are looking for: **Applicants with:- A very good university degree in mathematics, computational science, engineering, or a closely related field;- A strong interest in numerical analysis, optimization, partial differential equations, or scientific computing;- A willingness to work on both the mathematical analysis and the implementation of numerical methods for PDE-constrained optimization problems;- Good communication skills and the ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in an interdisciplinary research environment;- Good written and spoken English skills.Desirable Qualifications:Experience in one or more of the following areas is an advantage but not a requirement:- Finite element methods, adaptive methods, or a posteriori error estimation;- Convex analysis, nonsmooth optimization, or optimal control;- PDE-constrained optimization or inverse problems;- Numerical methods for elasticity, structural mechanics, or related models;- Implementation of numerical methods in Python, MATLAB, Julia, C/C++, or finite element software.What we offer:- The opportunity to work at WIAS Berlin, a leading research institution with strengths in partial differential equations, mathematical modeling, nonlinear optimization, and applied mathematics in general;- The option of mobile working;- A certified family-friendly work environment (Audit berufundfamilie);- The opportunity to live and work in Berlin, one of the world's most culturally rich and diverse international cities. Berlin offers a wide range of opportunities to enjoy life outside work while remaining relatively affordable compared with other major cities. Neither the position nor living in Berlin requires knowledge of German, although WIAS offers free German courses. We particularly welcome international applicants. Berlin also offers a rich scientific landscape, with numerous research opportunities and career prospects in both academia and industry;- Close mentorship from the supervisor and other peers through a dedicated mentorship program.Please direct scientific queries to Prof Dr. Michael Hintermüller (michael.hintermueller@wias-berlin.de).The appointment is limited to two years. The position is full-time (39 hours per week), with a salary based on pay grade E 13 of the German TVöD Bund pay scale.WIAS is committed to fostering diversity and equal opportunities and particularly encourages women to apply. Applicants with disabilities will be given preferential consideration in cases of equal qualification. If you have any questions or want to provide us with information related to diversity, inclusion or disabilities, please feel free to consult our website orcontact our Diversity Officer, Sara Krummenacher (sara.krummenacher@wias-berlin.de).How to apply:Please upload your complete application documents (motivation letter, detailed CV, certificates, copy of the master thesis, etc.) via our applicant portal using the button “Apply online”.The application period opens immediately and remains open until the position is filled.We are looking forward to your application!

jobs.occupation: Program Manager – Project Digitalization & Data Integration (f/m/d) (IT-Manager/in)

jobs.description: A Snapshot of Your Day Join us in transforming how our EPC projects access and use information. You will lead BIM Recalibration@GS SO, advance reliable information flows and digital interfaces, and drive adoption of improved ways of working. Alongside this, you will steer our broader data integration activities, provide clear business direction and align the roadmap with the overarching GS Data Backbone initiative. Your work will enable project teams and operational BIM Managers through consistent practices, trusted information and practical digital solutions.How You’ll Make an Impact * Identify and prioritize information management use cases and project information needs, mapping information producers, consumers, source systems and exchange points along the EPC project lifecycle* Lead BIM Recalibration@GS SO and translate its outcomes into practical, repeatable processes and workflows with clear responsibilities and handovers, embedding improved ways of working across projects* Drive the continuous development of information management practices and information flows across the data landscape, defining requirements for reliable data flows and digital interfaces and guiding implementation with solution architects, digital teams and tool owners, grounded in ISO 19650 principles* Lead communication, training and rollout support so colleagues understand, adopt and sustain new processes and digital practices* Shape and steer GS SO's broader data integration roadmap, aligning priorities and dependencies with the GS Data Backbone initiative and connecting information management and wider EPC needs to reusable data capabilities; guide shared data definitions, cross-system mapping, source-of-truth rules, ownership and quality expectations with data owners, stewards and technical specialists* Track implementation, adoption and business benefits across both areas, using project feedback to improve processes, evaluate new integration approaches with specialists and scale proven solutionsWhat You Bring* A degree in engineering, business informatics, digitalization or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience* Several years of experience leading cross-functional programs, process improvement or data-integration initiatives, ideally in energy, engineering, construction or other complex project environments* The ability to understand what information EPC teams need, where it is created and used, and how it should move between tools and project phases, and to turn this into clear requirements and governed processes for solution architects and technical teams* A strong conceptual and practical understanding of how data is stored, connected and made usable across tools, including relational storage, knowledge graphs, tool-specific and cross-tool/domain ontologies, semantic layers, replication and ingestion, and platforms such as Snowflake* The ability to establish rules that identify the same object across systems, harmonize values, determine the valid source, validate completeness and quality, and retain traceability, alongside practical knowledge of BIM methodology and ISO 19650* Strong stakeholder and change-management skills, a structured delivery mindset, very good English and good German communication skillsAbout the TeamAt Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.      Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideoOur Commitment to Diversity Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences. Rewards/Benefits * In addition to an attractive remuneration package in line with the market, you can expect an attractive employer-financed company pension scheme* We also offer the opportunity to become a Siemens Energy shareholder* We offer our employees the opportunity to work flexibly and remotely, and our inspiring offices provide space for collaboration and creativity* The professional and personal development of our employees is very important to us. We provide them with the opportunities to learn and develop in a self-determined way, various attractive programmes and learning materials are available for this purpose* In relation to the "compatibility of family and work", we have a wide range of offers, e.g. flexible working time models, childcare places at many locations, the possibility of trial part-time work or even a sabbaticalWe value equal opportunities and welcome applications from people with disabilities.https://jobs.siemens-energy.com/jobs

Experience with solid-state or particle characterization, imaging or laboratory automation is advantageous.- Sound understanding of oral drug absorption and its relationship to drug substance properties, formulation performance and gastrointestinal conditions. German language skills are advantageous but not required.As part of our commitment to transparency and fairness, salary information will be shared during the recruitment process.
